intro: Your tense roadmap from A1 to early B1. Each card shows when to use the tense and examples in 🌎 Latin American and 🇪🇸 Spain Spanish.

tenses.name: Present (regular)
when: Facts and routines
What's happening now
Near future plans (“Ceno con Javi esta noche”)

tenses.name: Present (irregular & stem-changing)
when: The most common verbs – ser, estar, tener, ir, hacer, querer, poder…
tenses.formation: tengo, voy, hago, soy, estoy · e → ie (empiezo) · o → ue (vuelvo) – nosotros/vosotros don't change

examples.latam: Tengo dos hermanos y voy a la universidad a pie.
examples.en: I have two siblings and I walk to university.

examples.latam: Mis clases empiezan a las diez.

tenses.name: Ser vs estar
when: Ser: identity, origin, job, personality, time
Estar: feelings, temporary states, location
tenses.formation: ser: soy, eres, es, somos, sois 🇪🇸, son · estar: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis 🇪🇸, están

examples.latam: Diego es de México y es muy simpático.
examples.en: Diego is from Mexico and he's very nice.

examples.latam: Hoy está cansado y está en casa.
examples.en: Today he's tired and he's at home.

tenses.name: Gustar-type verbs
when: Likes and dislikes, things you love (encantar), things that interest you (interesar)
tenses.formation: me / te / le / nos / os 🇪🇸 / les + gusta (one thing, verb) or gustan (several things)

examples.latam: Me gusta la salsa, pero me encantan los boleros.
examples.en: I like salsa, but I love boleros.

tenses.name: Simple past
when: Finished actions at a specific time in the past
In Latin America: also for things that happened today
The main events of a story

examples.latam: El verano pasado viajé a Colombia.
examples.en: Last summer I travelled to Colombia.
Today I ate / have eaten paella.

tenses.spainNote: Spain uses the pretérito for clearly finished time periods (ayer, el año pasado, en 2019), but switches to the pretérito perfecto for today, this week, this year and life experiences.

tenses.name: Present perfect
when: 🇪🇸 Spain: anything that happened today, this week, this year
Both: life experiences (“¿Has estado en México?”)
Both: ya / todavía no (already / not yet)
tenses.formation: haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis 🇪🇸, han) + participle (-ado / -ido): he comido, has viajado

examples.en: Have you ever been to Mexico?

examples.spain: Esta mañana he ido al mercado.
examples.en: This morning I went to the market.

tenses.spainNote: Around Alcalá and Madrid you'll hear this constantly: “¿Qué has hecho hoy?” – “He ido a clase y he comido con Lucía.”

tenses.name: Imperfect
when: Describing the past: how things were, background
Habits: what you used to do
Age, time and weather in the past

examples.latam: Cervantes nació en Alcalá cuando la universidad era muy importante.
examples.en: Cervantes was born in Alcalá when the university was very important.

examples.latam: De niña, iba a la playa todos los veranos.
examples.en: As a girl, I used to go to the beach every summer.

tenses.name: Pretérito vs imperfecto
when: Imperfecto = the scene, the background, what WAS happening
Pretérito = the event, what HAPPENED
Often together with mientras / cuando
tenses.formation: Mientras + imperfecto, … pretérito: “Mientras esperaba el tren, vi a Javi.”

examples.latam: Mientras caminaba por la calle Mayor, vi una cigüeña enorme.
examples.en: While I was walking down the Calle Mayor, I saw a huge stork.
It was raining when we arrived in Madrid.

tenses.name: Near future
when: Plans and intentions
Things that are about to happen
The most common way to talk about the future in conversation
tenses.formation: ir (voy, vas, va, vamos, vais 🇪🇸, van) + a + infinitive

examples.latam: En febrero voy a tener conversaciones reales en español.
examples.en: In February I'm going to have real conversations in Spanish.

examples.latam: ¿Qué van a hacer el fin de semana?
examples.spain: ¿Qué vais a hacer el fin de semana?
examples.en: What are you (all) going to do at the weekend?

pastCompare.title: Talking about today: Hoy comí 🌎 vs Hoy he comido 🇪🇸

latam.label: this morning
latam.en: This morning I went to the market.

spain.label: this morning
spain.text: Esta mañana he ido al mercado.
spain.en: This morning I went to the market.

pastCompare.note: Both are correct and understood everywhere. Use the 🌎 form with Latin American friends and expect to hear the 🇪🇸 form all day in Alcalá. For yesterday and earlier, both regions use the pretérito: “Ayer comí paella.”

timeline:
Quick decision guide:
• Happening now / routine → presente
• Finished event (yesterday, last year) → pretérito
• Today / this week in Spain, or life experience → pretérito perfecto
• Background, description, “used to” → imperfecto
• Plans → ir a + infinitivo
